questions.q: The actual value of resistance $R$ , shown in the figure is $30Ω .$ This is measured in an experiment as shown using the standard formula $R = \dfrac{V}{I}$ , where $V$ and $I$ are the readings of the voltmeter and ammeter, respectively. If the measured value of $R$ is $5%$ less, then the internal resistance of the voltmeter is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Measured value of $R = 5 %$ less than
actual value of~$R$ i.e., $R^{'} = 30 - ( 5 %$ of~$30) = 30 - \dfrac{5}{100} \times 30$

$R^{'} = 28 . 5Ω$~$. . . \left(i\right)$

Now, let us assume that internal resistance of voltmeter ${R}_{V}$. Replacing voltmeter with its internal resistance, we get following circuit.

It is clear that the measured value, $R^{'}$ should be equal to parallel combination of $R$~and ${R}_{V}$. Mathematically,
$R^{'} = $\dfrac{R \times {R}_{V}}{R + {R}_{V}} =$28 . 5Ω$

Given. $R = 30Ω$

$⇒ $\dfrac{30{R}_{V}}{30 + {R}_{V}} =$28 . 5$

$⇒ 30{R}_{V} = \left(28 . 5 \times30\right) + 28 . 5{R}_{V}$

$⇒ 1 . 5{R}_{V} = 28 . 5 \times30$

$⇒ {R}_{V} = $\dfrac{28 . 5 \times 30}{1 . 5} =$19 \times30$

or ${R}_{V} = 570Ω

$

questions.q: If $n$ represents the actual number of deflections in a converted galvanometer of resistance $G$ and shunt resistance $S$. Then the total current $I$ when its figure of merit is $K$ will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let current through galvanometer be ${I}_{G}$ and current through shunt resistance be $I - {I}_{G}$.

Given figure of merit $K = \dfrac{{I}_{G}}{n}$

Then, total current, $I = \dfrac{{I}_{G}\left(G + S\right)}{S}$

$I = \dfrac{nK\left(G + S\right)}{S}$

questions.q: The drift velocity of electrons for a conductor connected in an electrical circuit is ${V}_{d}$. The conductor is now replaced by another conductor with same material and same length but double the area of cross-section. The applied voltage remains same. The new drift velocity of electrons will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Drift velocity of electrons through a conductor kept in an external electric field& is given by& ${V}_{d} = - \dfrac{eE}{m}τ = - \dfrac{eV}{ml}τ$~

Where,~$e =$magnitude of charge on electron,~$m =$mass of electron,~$E =$external electric field and~$τ =$average relaxation time.

As, drift velocity is independent of area. So, the new drift velocity of electrons will be~${V}_{d}$.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $100Ω$ has $50$ divisions on its scale and has sensitivity of $20\muA / division$ . It is to be converted to voltmeter with three ranges, of $0 - 2V, 0 - 10V$ and $0 - 20V .$ The appropriate circuit to do so is:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, the resistance of the galvanometer& $G = 100Ω$
No. of divisions $= 50$
Current Sensitivity $= 20\muA / division$

The maximum current through galvanometer will be~
${I}_\max = 50 \times 20 \times {10}^{- 6} = {10}^{- 3}A$
For ${V}_{1} = 2V$

using Ohm's law~${V}_{1} = {I}_\max \left(G + {R}_{1}\right)$
$2 = {10}^{- 3} \times \left(100 + {R}_{1}\right)$
$∴ {R}_{1} = 1900Ω$

For ${V}_{2} = 10V$

using Ohm's law~${V}_{2} = {I}_\max \left(G + {R}_{1} + {R}_{2}\right)$

$10 = {10}^{- 3} \times \left(100 + 1900 + {R}_{2}\right)$
$∴ {R}_{2} = 8000Ω$

For ${V}_{3} = 20V$

using Ohm's law~${V}_{3} = {I}_\max \left(G + {R}_{1} + {R}_{2} + {R}_{3}\right)$
$20 = {10}^{- 3} \left(100 + 1900 + 8000 + {R}_{3}\right)$
$∴ {R}_{3} = 10 \times {10}^{3}Ω$

questions.q: A $72Ω$ galvanometer is shunted by a resistance of $8Ω$. The percentage of the total current which passes through the galvanometer is&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let& $G$ be resistance of galvanometer and $I '$~be the current passing through the galvanometer produces full scale deflection. If $I$ is the maximum current, and since, $G$ and~$S$ are in parallel so, the potential difference between them will be same.

Then,

~$I^{'}G = {I}_{2}S ⇒ 72I^{'} = 8{I}_{2} ⇒ {I}_{2} = 9I^{'} ⇒ I = I^{'} + {I}_{2} = 10I^{'}$

So the percentage of total current passes through galvanometer~is~

$\dfrac{I '}{I} \times 100= \dfrac{I '}{10I^{'}} \times 100 = 10 %$

questions.q: In the given circuit, the current flowing through the resistance $20Ω$ is $0 . 3A$, while the ammeter reads $0 . 9A$. The value of ${R}_{1}$ is _____Ω.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, ${i}_{1} = 0 . 3A, {i}_{1} + {i}_{2} + {i}_{3} = 0 . 9A$

So, ${V}_{AB} = {i}_{1} \times 20Ω = 0 . 3 \times 20V = 6V$

${i}_{2} = \dfrac{6V}{15Ω} = \dfrac{2}{5}A$

Now,

${i}_{1} + {i}_{2} + {i}_{3} = \dfrac{9}{10}A$

$⇒ \dfrac{3}{10} + \dfrac{2}{5} + {i}_{3} = \dfrac{9}{10}$

$⇒ \dfrac{7}{10} + {i}_{3} = \dfrac{9}{10}$

$⇒ {i}_{3} = 0 . 2A$

So, ${i}_{3} \times {R}_{1} = 6V$

$⇒ ( 0 . 2 ) {R}_{1} = 6$

$⇒ {R}_{1} = \dfrac{6}{0 . 2} = 30Ω$

questions.q: $10$ resistors each of resistance $10 Ω$ can be connected in such as to get maximum and minimum equivalent resistance. The ratio of maximum and minimum equivalent resistance will be________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When all the resistors are connected in series, the total resistance is

${R}_\max = 10R$

$⇒ {R}_\max = 10 \times 10 = 100Ω$

When all the resistors are connected in parallel, the total resistance is

~${R}_\min = \dfrac{R}{10}$

$⇒ {R}_\min = \dfrac{10}{10} = 1Ω$

Hence, the ratio,

~$\dfrac{Rmax}{Rmin} = \dfrac{100Ω}{1Ω} = 100$.

questions.q: Two coils require $20$ minutes and $60$ minutes respectively to produce same amount of heat energy when connected separately to the same source. If they are connected in parallel arrangement to the same source; the time required to produce same amount of heat by the combination of coils, will be _____~$min$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If& $H$~is the heat required to heat the water, then

${P}_{1} \times 60 = H ⇒ {P}_{1} = \dfrac{H}{60}$~and~${P}_{2} \times 20 = H ⇒ {P}_{2} = \dfrac{H}{20}$

When the coils are connected in parallel their powers will get added. If the required time now is~$t$, then

\left({P}_{1} + {P}_{2}\right)t = H ⇒ t = \dfrac{H}{\dfrac{H}{60} + \dfrac{H}{20}} = 15min$

$
